source_context_translations.translation: Weaken their resolve and strengthen their bones.
So that even the wise do not dare to act.
Practice nonaction, and nothing will be left ungoverned.

The Way is empty, and though used it is never filled; how deep it is, like the ancestor of all things! It blunts its sharpness, untangles its confusions, tempers its brightness, and mingles with its dust. How still it is, as if it might endure.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): Having little strength, force, or vitality.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Describes an inherent state rather than an action.
additional_senses.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text with Wang Bi commentary
Sentence Translations (English): The people are weak and have few desires.
When an army is weak, it is defeated.
Because people are weak, they seek help from the Way.
The weak waters do not contend.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To make something less strong, less forceful, or less intense.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Used causatively: it means reducing the force or vigor of what follows.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text with Wang Bi commentary

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The inward intention, purpose, or determination that directs a person's mind and actions.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): In this kind of prose it points to settled inward purpose rather than mere momentary desire.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text with Wang Bi commentary

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): Having great strength, force, or resistance.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Describes an existing quality, not an action.
additional_senses.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text with Wang Bi commentary
Sentence Translations (English): When troops are strong, they win.
His resolve is strong and unbending.
When water is strong, it rushes fiercely.
When the state is strong, the people are at peace.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To make something stronger, more powerful, or more durable.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Causative use: the subject brings strength to what follows.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text with Wang Bi commentary

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The hard framework of the body; by extension, bodily strength or frame.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it is concrete, and in such passages it often implies the physical frame as the seat of bodily strength.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text with Wang Bi commentary

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A person who is intelligent, prudent, and capable of sound judgment.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Refers to a person characterized by intelligence or wisdom, often with an implied social or moral valuation.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text with Wang Bi commentary

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To have enough boldness, permission, or confidence to do something.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Usually followed by an action that is undertaken only if one feels bold enough or entitled to do it.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text with Wang Bi commentary

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A sentence-final particle that marks a statement, often lending a confirming or expository tone.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): In this text it helps give the clause a completed, declarative finish.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text with Wang Bi commentary

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A connective marking consequence or result: if the prior condition is met, the following outcome holds.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Introduces the result of the preceding condition or state.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text with Wang Bi commentary

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To move forward forcefully and quickly, especially into or against something.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Implies forceful forward motion, often with impact.
Sentence Translations (English): The horse charged into the battle line.
The boat surged through the waves.
The chariot rushed forward without stopping.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Lacking fullness or solidity; open, unfilled, and receptive.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): In Laozi this often suggests productive emptiness or openness rather than mere absence.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; likely early Laozi base text as transmitted in Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): The practical role, purpose, or effect of a thing.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Focuses on what something is for or how it operates, not the act of using it.
additional_senses.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text with Wang Bi commentary
Sentence Translations (English): If one knows its function, one can accomplish things.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To put something into operation, make use of it, or draw practical effect from it.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it is the practical application of what is present in the Way.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; likely early Laozi base text as transmitted in Wang Bi recension
